We need to implement function makeSmallestPalindrome that given a string s (len up to 1000) returns lexicographically smallest palindrome reachable with minimum operations.

Problem: We can replace characters with any lowercase letters; each replacement counts as one operation. We need to transform s into a palindrome with minimal number of changes. Among all palindromes achievable with minimal changes, we need the lexicographically smallest string.

This is typical: For each symmetric pair (i, n-1-i), we need to make them equal. If they are already equal, we don't change them (0 operations). If they differ, we need to change at least one of them to make them equal. Changing one character (either left or right) suffices: set both to one of the letters (the one from left or right). Minimal operations for each pair: 0 if already same; else 1.

Thus total minimal operations = number of mismatched pairs.

Now lexicographically smallest palindrome among those with minimal operations: For each mismatched pair, we must choose a letter to set both positions to; we have two options: either set to the smaller of the two letters? Wait we need to minimize lexicographic order globally. Since operations count is independent per pair (changing one char per mismatched pair), we can choose for each pair which letter to set both positions to (by changing the other char). If we set both to left char, we change right char; cost 1. If set both to right char, change left char; cost 1. So either way 1 operation.

But there is also option to change both to a third letter (cost 2) which would increase operations beyond minimal, so not allowed.

Thus to achieve minimal operations we must for each mismatched pair pick either left or right letter as the target.

Goal: produce lexicographically smallest resulting string after applying these decisions.

Observation: Lexicographic order depends on leftmost differing character. So we should try to make earlier positions as small as possible.
